name: Integration added with zero code
purpose: A new integration needs no per-integration code anywhere.
record: Case: add a fake integration (fake MCP server plus one catalog entry, with a fake icon, two scopes, one read tool, one write tool) through the catalog or hub alone. Steps: it appears in the catalog, a user connects it with a generated form or consent screen, the AI calls the read tool, the write tool waits for approval, the user disconnects. Count: files changed that name the fake integration in the frontend, the backend and the AI runner (target 0 each); lines of code added per layer (target 0); steps that needed a human edit (target 0). Draft: no run exists yet.
disadvantages: A fake integration proves the catalog path, not that every real integration's quirks fit it.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=tests/test_registry.py passes with a fake hub accepted by configuration alone]

name: Integration available within the weekly refresh
purpose: A new integration reaches users within the weekly refresh.
record: Per integration a hub lists: days from the hub listing date to the first successful user connect in a test account (target at most 7, the weekly refresh). Read from catalog sync timestamps, never estimated. Draft: no run exists yet.
disadvantages: It measures time to a first user connection, so it does not see an integration that connects but cannot be used.

name: Integration credentials stay with their user
purpose: One user's integration never reaches another user's turn.
record: Checks, each pass or fail (target all pass): user B's turn lists none of user A's connected servers; a tool call forged with A's connection id from B's session is refused; stored credentials are encrypted and absent from every API response, log line and prompt; a disconnect removes the credential and the server from the next turn; a write tool never runs without an approval record. Draft: no run exists yet.
disadvantages: The checks are pass or fail on the cases written, so a leak path nobody wrote a check for goes unseen.

name: Cards found again, none lost
purpose: A card that was added is found again by its words, and adding the same id twice loses nothing.
record: Cases passed over written add and search sequences.
disadvantages: Does not test scale or several writers at once.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=tests/test_cardstore.py passes and the written add and search cases pass; the store calls no model, so the whole set runs at no cost]

name: Integration served by combined hubs
purpose: An integration is served by the combination of hubs that covers the most of it.
record: The share of an app's actions covered by the catalog entry, counting every hub it names.

name: Balanced score of a builder's cards on file-finding, topic and orientation cases, with the store's size
purpose: A card groups information on one topic from many files, so a card builder is judged by one number: whether its cards serve a mix of cases (finding a file, the files a topic task needed, the neighbourhood of a file) from a store small enough to be topic cards, at a price in money and time a team would pay.
record: Per builder, the balanced score (accuracy, cost and time; [balance.cards_from_files]), one number per arm per stage. The case set mixes three kinds with the weights of evaluation/cards_from_files/mix.py: the file-finding tasks (right when the needed file is among the first three files of the view), topic tasks taken from the git history of the consumer whose subject names no file or identifier (right when half of the files the commit changed are inside the first three cards; a builder learns only from older commits), and the orientation proxy (right when a file of the target's folder is among the first three files). Store size is a term of the number: a store near one card per file, or over the card limit of the store, gives up that share of every case, so a card per file scores nothing and is a baseline, never promoted. The view is the picked cards in rank order, each card's files in the builder's own order. In the details: each kind's raw result and counted cases, the store penalty and cards per file, the topic coverage of the first card and of the first three, their noise and bundling across folders, cards built, the build's id, its model calls, tokens, cost and seconds (charged to the first scored case), and the cost of bootstrapping from the sources, which belongs to the builder and not to a retrieval arm: the files and megabytes the build read under the corpus root, the reads per file ingested, and for a builder that calls no model the reads and seconds of a refresh over the unchanged corpus and their share of the full build's (1.0 is a full rescan, a small share is an incremental refresh).
disadvantages: The cases ask about one Python repository, so a builder good at prose folders is not measured; subjects are developer language written for a commit, some files were renamed later, and the corpus is the pinned state while the topic tasks are earlier; the selector is keyword IDF, not production's hybrid, because the vector half needs an authorized embedding run; coverage is the right files in front of the reader, not an answer found; the mix and the store penalty are set by value and a later set of real inputs should calibrate them; the build's source reads are reported and not yet priced into the number (the corpus is a local folder, so a read is cheap here), and the staleness lag of a changed source is not measured because the corpus is pinned; the library's balanced score has three terms, so the store term is applied to the accuracy inside the scorer.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new builder is described: rate it on the five questions of the scale before it is built] > free [sample=full | real=no | gate=competitive | when=the builders that call no model, and the replay of the saved paid build, build cards for the pinned corpus and the fixed selector ranks every case of the mix: seconds, and the stage to iterate in] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=a builder that calls a model beat the best free arm on the free stage: it builds cards for the pinned corpus, with a cassette of its model calls where the harness offers one, and the cards and the ranking of one case are read by hand] > sample [sample=sample:10 | real=yes | gate=competitive | when=the one-case stage passed: the same build ranks a sample of cases spread over the areas of the code] > whole [sample=full | real=yes | gate=competitive | when=one full paid run, only for a variant that beat the best free arm on the sample, compared on the same number with every other builder]
